mainTopic: Why חזקיה and רבי יוחנן can argue about a basket (קופה) with a שרץ inside, when שמאי and הלל seem to agree that such a basket is טמא retroactively. The answer narrows their argument to a basket that was examined, or, in a second answer, to a basket that was covered.
overview: This amud keeps working on a contradiction. שמאי and הלל seem to agree that a basket of טהרות with a שרץ found in it is טמא going back in time, so how can חזקיה call the food טהור? The גמרא first answers that חזקיה and רבי יוחנן argue about a basket that was examined. It then gives a second answer: they argue about a basket that was covered. Each answer is challenged because the basket must match a woman, and each time the reply is that blood is so common in a woman that she counts as unexamined or uncovered. A third answer says the basket was moved from one corner of a house to another. חזקיה does not assume the טומאה moved with it from place to place, and רבי יוחנן does. The גמרא then challenges רבי יוחנן from a teaching that טומאה is judged by the time and the place where it is found. It tries to say that rule only stops us from burning תרומה but still leaves it on hold. That idea is rejected with the rusty needle and the burned שרץ. A new distinction, between items that stayed put and items that moved, is attacked with the case of a loaf that fell past an impure item and is still pure. The amud ends as the גמרא starts to explain that the loaf case has its own reason, and that explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: חזקיה and רבי יוחנן argue only about an examined basket
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer. The argument between חזקיה and רבי יוחנן is about a basket that was checked. חזקיה relies on the check, and רבי יוחנן worries the שרץ fell in right as the checker pulled his hand out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where חזקיה and רבי יוחנן disagree is about a basket that was examined. One holds: he examined it, so it was clean. The other holds: say that it fell in just as he was pulling his hand out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its answer to the contradiction. שמאי and הלל agree about an unchecked basket, but חזקיה and רבי יוחנן argue about a basket that was checked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This removes the contradiction, because now the two arguments are about different cases. For חזקיה, the check proves the basket was clean, so the שרץ must have come in later. For רבי יוחנן, the check is not good enough, because the שרץ could have dropped in the moment the checker's hand left the basket.

keyTerms.meaning: A basket, here one used to hold pure food (טהרות)
One master holds (introduces each side of an argument)

phrases.english: Where Chizkiya and Rabbi Yochanan disagree
is regarding a basket that was examined.
One master holds: he did examine it,
phrases.notes: This is חזקיה: since it was checked and clean, the שרץ must have come in later.

phrases.english: and the other master holds: say that
right as he removed his hand, it fell in.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי פְּלִיגִי חִזְקִיָּה וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בְּקוּפָּה בְּדוּקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun just before this section: שמאי and הלל agree about an unexamined basket.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each argument is placed in a different case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It looked as if חזקיה disagreed with what both שמאי and הלל agree on about the basket.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמאי and הלל spoke about an unexamined basket. חזקיה and רבי יוחנן argue only about an examined one.

steps.title: But the basket is compared to a woman, and a woman is examined
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. הלל's basket is supposed to be like a woman, and a woman checks herself. So הלל's basket must also be an examined basket.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the basket is taught as being similar to a woman, and a woman is examined!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. The basket case was brought as a parallel to a woman, and a woman is someone who checks herself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If הלל's basket must match the woman, it should be an examined basket too. Then שמאי and הלל would be agreeing about an examined basket, and חזקיה would contradict them again.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught as similar to a woman,
phrases.notes: הלל used the basket to make a point about a woman who finds blood.

phrases.english: and a woman is examined!

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שמאי and הלל spoke about an unexamined basket.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The basket must be like the woman. A woman is examined, so the basket in their case is examined too.

steps.title: A woman counts as unexamined because blood is common
steps.stepSummary: Since women regularly see blood, a woman is treated as if she were not examined. So she matches an unexamined basket.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since blood is commonly found in her, she is like one who is not examined.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends its answer. Because blood regularly comes from a woman, her checks do not make her count as 'examined.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood can come at any moment, so a past check does not give much security. That is why the woman fits with an unexamined basket, and the first answer stands.

phrases.english: Since blood is commonly found in her,
she is like one who is not examined.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the woman is treated as unexamined.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A woman checks herself, so she should count as examined.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because blood is common, she counts as unexamined, so she matches an unexamined basket.
steps.whatToRemember: First answer: שמאי and הלל agree about an unexamined basket, and a woman counts as unexamined because blood is common. חזקיה and רבי יוחנן argue about an examined basket.

steps.title: Second answer: uncovered basket versus covered basket
steps.stepSummary: Another way to remove the contradiction. שמאי and הלל agree about a basket that is not covered, while חזקיה and רבי יוחנן argue about a covered basket.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: where שמאי and הלל agree is about a basket that is not covered. Where חזקיה and רבי יוחנן disagree is about a covered basket.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second, different way to explain the contradiction. This time the difference between the cases is whether the basket was covered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An uncovered basket could easily have had a שרץ fall in at any time, so everyone agrees it is טמא going back in time. A covered basket is better protected, so there is room to argue about when the שרץ got in.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (introduces another answer)

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
where Shammai and Hillel agree
is about a basket that is not covered;
where Chizkiya and Rabbi Yochanan disagree
is about a basket that is covered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer instead of the examined/unexamined split.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases a different way: covered versus uncovered.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חזקיה seems to contradict what שמאי and הלל agree on.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמאי and הלל spoke about an uncovered basket. חזקיה and רבי יוחנן argue about a covered one.

steps.title: How could a שרץ get into a covered basket?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a שרץ could fall into a basket that is covered.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is covered, how did it fall in?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the new case: a covered basket seems sealed, so how did the שרץ get inside?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not an attack on the answer. It asks us to picture a realistic case where a covered basket could still end up with a שרץ inside.

phrases.english: If it is covered, how did it fall in?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the practical case in the second answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can a שרץ end up inside a covered basket?

steps.title: A basket used by opening its lid
steps.stepSummary: The case is a basket that is used by taking the lid off and putting it back. While it was open, a שרץ could have fallen in.
steps.simpleTranslation: For example, where it is used by means of the cover, meaning it is opened and closed for use.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the basket is normally covered, but it gets opened whenever someone uses it, so a שרץ could fall in then.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the argument makes sense. חזקיה assumes the שרץ came in after the food was taken out, since a person is careful while the food is inside. רבי יוחנן worries it slipped in during one of the openings without anyone noticing.

phrases.english: For example, where it is used by way of its cover.
phrases.notes: He means you take the lid off to use it, so for a moment it is open.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The basket is opened by removing the lid each time it is used, so a שרץ could fall in during use.

steps.title: But a woman is like a covered basket
steps.stepSummary: The same kind of challenge comes back. The basket must be like a woman, and a woman is 'covered,' since no blood gets in from outside. So הלל's basket should be covered too.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the basket is taught as similar to a woman, and a woman is covered!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second answer the same way it challenged the first: the basket must match a woman, and a woman seems 'covered.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a woman is like a covered basket, then שמאי and הלל were talking about a covered basket. In that case חזקיה would contradict them again.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught as similar to a woman,
and a woman is covered!
phrases.notes: Nothing comes into her from outside, so she is like a closed container.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second answer (steps 4–6), just as step 2 challenged the first.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שמאי and הלל spoke about an uncovered basket.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The basket must be like the woman. A woman is covered, so the basket in their case is covered too.

steps.title: A woman counts as uncovered because blood is common
steps.stepSummary: Since blood regularly comes from a woman, she is treated as if she were uncovered. So she matches an uncovered basket.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since blood is commonly found in her, she is like one who is not covered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the second answer with the same reasoning as before: because blood is common in a woman, she counts as 'not covered.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being sealed from outside does not help when the blood comes from inside her and comes often. So the woman matches an uncovered basket, and the second answer stands.

phrases.english: Since blood is commonly found in her,
she is like one who is not covered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 7, using the same reasoning as step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the woman is treated as uncovered.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A woman is sealed from the outside, so she should count as covered.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because blood is common, she counts as uncovered, so she matches an uncovered basket.
steps.whatToRemember: Two answers, one pattern: שמאי and הלל agree about a weak case (an unexamined or uncovered basket), and חזקיה and רבי יוחנן argue about a stronger case (examined or covered). Each time, the woman fits the weak case because blood is common in her.

steps.title: Another answer: a basket's corner versus a house's corner
steps.stepSummary: A new way to remove the contradiction: שמאי and הלל agree about the corner of a basket, while חזקיה and רבי יוחנן argue about the corner of a house.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say this: when שמאי and הלל agree, it is about the corner of a basket. When חזקיה and רבי יוחנן argue, it is about the corner of a house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one more way to answer the contradiction. It says the two arguments are about two different places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answers split the cases by examined versus unexamined baskets (steps 1-3) and by covered versus uncovered baskets (steps 4-8). Now the split is by location. A spot inside the basket is where שמאי and הלל agree, and a spot in the house is where חזקיה and רבי יוחנן argue.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
When שמאי and הלל agree,
it is about the corner of a basket;
when חזקיה and רבי יוחנן disagree,
it is about the corner of a house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new answer instead of the covered/uncovered distinction of steps 4-8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: the two arguments are about different locations.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two arguments seemed to be about the same case, so they seemed to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמאי and הלל speak about a basket's corner, while חזקיה and רבי יוחנן speak about a house's corner.

steps.title: But the case was about a basket
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the argument of חזקיה and רבי יוחנן was clearly stated about a basket, not about a house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the new answer. The argument of חזקיה and רבי יוחנן was about a basket, so how can we say it is about a house?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new answer only works if their argument is about a house. But the wording we have says 'basket.' So the answer seems to go against the actual words.

keyTerms.meaning: But look. It introduces a challenge.

phrases.english: But it says "basket"!
phrases.notes: This is pointing back to how the argument of חזקיה and רבי יוחנן was stated earlier: about a basket.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 9 based on the wording of the earlier statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 9 that חזקיה and רבי יוחנן argue about the corner of a house.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The original statement of their argument explicitly speaks of a basket.

steps.title: A basket moved from one corner of the house to another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the case involves a basket that held טהרות in one corner and was then moved to another corner, where a שרץ was found in it. חזקיה does not assume the טומאה moved from place to place. רבי יוחנן does.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: a basket was used for pure items in this corner of the house. Then it was moved to another corner, and a שרץ was found in it in the other corner. חזקיה holds that we do not assume טומאה moved from one place to another. רבי יוחנן holds that we do.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection. The case really is about a basket, but the basket was moved between corners of a house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both 'basket' and 'house' are now true. The question is whether the שרץ found in the second corner is assumed to have already been in the basket back in the first corner, while the pure food was inside. חזקיה says no, so the food stays pure. רבי יוחנן says yes, so the food is impure.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means. It explains the true meaning of an earlier statement.
A dead creeping creature, which makes things טמא

steps.whatToRemember: חזקיה: we do NOT assume טומאה moved from place to place. רבי יוחנן: we DO assume it.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
a basket in which pure items were kept
in this corner of the house,
and they moved it to another corner,
and a שרץ was found in it in the other corner.
חזקיה holds:
we do not presume that impurity moved from place to place;
and רבי יוחנן holds: we do presume.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 10 by explaining that the basket case happened in a house.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case: the basket was moved between corners of a house.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case seemed to be only about a basket, with no house involved.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a basket moved within a house. The argument is whether we assume the טומאה moved with it from place to place.

steps.title: Do we really assume טומאה moved? A משנה about touching someone at night
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רבי יוחנן's view by quoting a משנה. Someone touched a person at night without knowing if he was alive or dead, and found him dead in the morning. רבי מאיר rules the toucher pure. חכמים rule him impure, because all טומאות are judged as they were at the time they are found.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do we really assume this? But we learned in a משנה: if someone touched a person at night and does not know if he was alive or dead, and the next morning he got up and found him dead, רבי מאיר says he is pure. חכמים say he is impure, because all טומאות are treated as they were at the time they were found.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's idea that we assume טומאה moved from place to place. It starts by quoting a משנה, and the full point of the challenge is explained in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר does not assume the man was already dead when he was touched, so the toucher is pure. חכמים do assume it, because a טומאה is judged as it was when it was found. This rule of חכמים is the base for the challenge, and the next step adds the words about place that actually hit רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: And do we really...? It introduces a challenging question.
As they were at the time they were found

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think this משנה alone disproves רבי יוחנן. Here חכמים are actually strict. The challenge only comes in the next step, where a teaching limits their rule to the place where the טומאה was found.

phrases.english: And do we presume this?
phrases.notes: This is aimed at רבי יוחנן, who said we assume the טומאה moved from place to place.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a משנה:
If someone touched a person at night,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ אִם חַי אִם מֵת,
phrases.english: and he does not know whether he was alive or dead,
and the next day he got up early and found him dead,
רבי מאיר rules him pure.
And חכמים rule him impure,
for all impurities are treated as they were at the time they were found.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's position from step 11, that we assume טומאה moved from place to place.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule: מחזקינן טומאה ממקום למקום.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה sets up the rule of חכמים: all טומאות are judged as they were at the time they were found. The next step quotes a teaching added to this משנה, that they are judged only in the place they were found. That addition is what goes against רבי יוחנן's presumption that טומאה moved from place to place.

steps.title: Judged by the time and the place of finding
steps.stepSummary: A teaching on the משנה adds that טומאה is judged both by the time and by the place where it is found. This challenges רבי יוחנן, who assumes the טומאה moved from another place.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a teaching was added to that משנה: impurities are judged as they were at the time they were found, and in the place they were found!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the question it started in Step 12. It quotes an extra teaching on that משנה, which says טומאה is judged by where it is found, not only when.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה alone only talked about time. The added teaching says place counts too: we do not assume the dead man was already dead in an earlier spot. That goes against רבי יוחנן, who assumes the שרץ was already in the basket's first corner.

keyTerms.meaning: In the place they are found: we do not assume the טומאה was somewhere else before.
On it, meaning a teaching added on top of the משנה just quoted.

phrases.english: And it is taught about it:
phrases.notes: "It" is the משנה from Step 12, about the person touched at night.

phrases.english: as at the time they are found,
and in the place they are found!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge opened in Step 12 by adding the decisive words about place.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that טומאה found in one corner of the basket is assumed to have been in the earlier corner too.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If טומאה is judged only in the place it is found, we may not assume the שרץ was in the corner where the טהרות were, so the טהרות should be pure.

steps.title: Maybe the rule only stops burning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a possible defense of רבי יוחנן. The 'place of finding' rule may only stop us from burning תרומה, while we still hold it 'on hold' out of doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: that rule is only about burning, but to leave things on hold, we do leave them on hold?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer for רבי יוחנן. Maybe the rule only means we can't treat the item as surely impure and burn it, but we still treat it as doubtful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two levels: surely impure (burn the תרומה) or doubtfully impure (leave it on hold, neither eaten nor burned). If the rule only blocks burning, רבי יוחנן could say the טהרות are at least doubtful because the טומאה may have moved.

keyTerms.meaning: To burn: treating תרומה as surely impure, so it must be burned.
To hang or leave on hold: doubtful תרומה is neither eaten nor burned.
And if you will say: introduces a possible answer the גמרא will test.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think 'on hold' means pure. Doubtful תרומה can't be eaten either. It just isn't burned.

phrases.english: And if you will say:
these words apply to burning,
phrases.notes: "These words" means the rule about the place of finding.

phrases.english: but to leave on hold, we do leave it on hold?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible way out of the challenge in Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the rule: it decides only 'surely impure', not 'doubtful'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'place of finding' rule makes the טהרות fully pure, against רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule only stops burning; the טהרות are still doubtful, which fits רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: The rusty needle proves we do not leave it on hold
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the defense. A משנה rules that a rusty or broken needle found on טהרות leaves them fully pure, even though it may have been a working needle earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: But do we really leave it on hold? We learned: a needle found full of rust or broken is pure, since all impurities are judged as at the time they are found. But why? Let's say it was a good needle at first and only now grew rust!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion from Step 14. It brings a משנה where we could have doubted, yet the ruling is simply 'pure,' not 'on hold.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rusty or broken needle cannot carry טומאה, but it may have been whole when it first touched the טהרות. If we left things on hold for possible earlier states, the משנה would say so. It says 'pure,' so this rule gives full purity, and the defense of רבי יוחנן fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Do we really leave it on hold? A strong rhetorical rejection.
A needle, here one that had been impure.
Rust. A needle full of rust no longer carries טומאה.

phrases.english: But do we leave it on hold?!
But didn't we learn in a משנה:
A needle that is found
phrases.notes: This needle had been impure and was found lying on טהרות.

phrases.english: full of rust or broken
is pure, for all impurities are judged as at the time they are found.
But why? Let us say:
this was originally a proper needle,
and only now did it grow rust.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 14 using a משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the 'time and place of finding' rule only stops burning but still leaves things on hold.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה about the needle rules the items fully pure, though an earlier impure state was possible. So this rule does not leave items on hold.

steps.title: Second proof: a burned שרץ on olives
steps.stepSummary: A second משנה backs up the rejection. A burned שרץ or a tattered rag found on olives leaves them fully pure, because impurities are judged as at the time they are found.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we also learned: if one found a burned שרץ on top of the olives, or a tattered rag, the olives are pure, since all impurities are judged as at the time they are found!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another משנה to strengthen its point from Step 15. Again the ruling is 'pure,' not 'on hold.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: A burned שרץ and a ragged cloth no longer spread טומאה, but they may have been whole when they landed on the olives. The משנה still says 'pure.' This confirms that the rule gives full purity, so רבי יוחנן cannot use the 'on hold' idea.

keyTerms.meaning: A burned creeping creature, which no longer passes on טומאה.
A tattered, worn-out rag that is too ragged to carry טומאה.
Olives, here the טהרות the item was found on.

steps.whatToRemember: The rule 'judge טומאה as at the time and place it is found' makes items fully pure, not just doubtful. Two משניות show this, the rusty needle and the burned שרץ, so the 'on hold' defense of רבי יוחנן fails.

phrases.english: And furthermore we learned:
If one found a burned שרץ
on top of the olives,
and likewise a tattered rag
phrases.notes: A rag from someone impure, now so worn it can no longer pass on טומאה.

phrases.english: they are pure, for all impurities are judged as at the time they are found!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second משנה supporting the rejection in Step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That the 'time of finding' rule leaves items fully pure and not on hold.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה: a burned שרץ or tattered rag found on olives leaves them pure.

steps.title: A new distinction: things that stayed put versus things that moved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the rule of judging טומאה by the time and place of finding works both ways only when the item stayed where it was found. When it came from another place, we do not burn the תרומה, but we hold it on hold.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: we judge things as at the time they are found, whether that leads to a leniency or a stringency, and in the place they are found. But when it is not the place where they were found, we do not burn, but we do hold it on hold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new way to save רבי יוחנן's view. It splits cases into ones where nothing moved and ones where something moved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the needle and rag cases from steps 15-16, nothing moved, so the 'time of finding' rule applies fully, even to make things pure. When something moved, as in רבי יוחנן's case, the 'place of finding' rule only stops us from burning. We still hold the item on hold because of the doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Whether it leads to a leniency or a stringency
We hold it on hold: we neither burn nor eat the doubtful תרומה

phrases.english: And if you would say: as at the time they are found
whether for a leniency or for a stringency
and that is in the place where they are found
but when it is not in the place where they are found
we do not burn
but we do hold it on hold

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refines the defense from step 14 so that it fits the needle and rag cases in steps 15-16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between cases where nothing moved and cases where something moved
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The needle and rag cases seemed to show that the 'time of finding' rule always settles things completely.
steps.terutzMaskana: Those cases involved no movement. Where something moved, we only hold it on hold, which fits רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: The loaf that fell past an impure item is still fully pure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: a loaf on a shelf with an impure item underneath, later found on the ground, is fully pure. We say a pure person came in and moved it. רבי אלעזר says this is true even on a sloped shelf.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn: a loaf was on top of a shelf, and an impure מדף was lying underneath it. Even though, if it fell, it could not have avoided touching it, the loaf is pure. For I say a pure person came in there and took it. This holds unless someone says, 'I am sure that no person came in there.' And רבי אלעזר said: this ruling was needed only for a sloped spot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the distinction from step 17. Here the loaf clearly moved from another place, yet it is ruled fully pure, not just held on hold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The loaf moved from the shelf to the ground, so by step 17's idea it should at least be held on hold. Instead it is fully pure, even on a sloped shelf where rolling off is very likely. So it seems that even when something moved, we do not suspect טומאה at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A lighter kind of impure item that can make food impure but not people or vessels
For I say: we assume an innocent explanation
A sloped place, where things easily roll off

steps.whyThisMatters: This case is exactly the kind רבי יוחנן cares about, where something moved. If it is fully pure, the 'hold it on hold' defense falls apart.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn: a loaf on top of a shelf
and an impure מדף lying underneath it
even though, if it fell

phrases.aramaic: אִי אֶפְשָׁר אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נָגְעָה — טְהוֹרָה
phrases.english: it could not have avoided touching it, it is pure
for I say that a pure person
came in there and took it

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיֹּאמַר: ״בָּרִי לִי שֶׁלֹּא נִכְנַס אָדָם שָׁם״
phrases.english: unless he says: 'I am certain that no person came in there'
And רבי אלעזר said:
it was needed only for a sloped spot!
phrases.notes: Even where the loaf most likely rolled off by itself, it is still pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the step 17 distinction with a case where something moved and is still fully pure.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that items which moved from another place are at least held on hold
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The loaf moved, and on a slope it very likely touched the impure item, yet it is fully pure and not held on hold.

steps.title: The loaf case has its own stated reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to answer that the loaf case proves nothing, because that ברייתא states its own special reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is as the reason is taught.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts pushing back against step 18. It is setting up the next move: the loaf ברייתא has a special reason that does not apply to other cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling of 'pure' in the loaf case does not come from a general rule about items that moved. It rests on the specific reason the ברייתא itself gives, so it cannot be used against step 17.

keyTerms.meaning: As its reason is explicitly taught

phrases.english: There, it is as the reason is taught
phrases.notes: The ברייתא's reason is 'שאני אומר אדם טהור נכנס לשם ונטלה': a pure person came in and moved it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends step 17 against step 18 by limiting the loaf ברייתא to its own reason.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to its own stated reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The loaf case seemed to show that moved items are never even held on hold.
steps.terutzMaskana: The loaf is pure only because of the specific reason the ברייתא gives, so it does not set a general rule.
